title: A straw poll after every round
allegory: The logit lens is like calling a straw poll after every round of a jury's deliberation: using the official counting rules, you ask 'if you had to vote right now, what would you say?', and watch when the verdict forms.

chapters.name: Deciding when?
chapters.note: 12 layers ... where did it make up its mind?

cap.1: A language model only speaks at the very end, after all its layers. You want to know when it actually made up its mind, and what it believed on the way.
cap.2: GPT-2 reads its residual stream through ln_final and W_U once, after the last block. Everything before that is hidden state with no obvious way to read it.
cap.3: We want a readout of intermediate residual states in output space: what distribution over tokens does the stream encode at depth L, before later layers write to it?

cap.1: Picture a jury deliberating in rounds. After each round you call a straw poll: 'If you had to vote right now, what would you say?' Nobody has to stop.
cap.2: The logit lens takes the residual stream after layer L and pushes it through the model's own final LayerNorm and unembedding, as if every later layer were deleted.
cap.3: Lens(L) = W_U · LN_final(resid_L). It works because the stream is one additive bus, so a partial sum is a legitimate object, and each token's unembedding direction is fixed.

cap.1: Take the notes after round L, format them the way the final round would be, and count votes with the official rules. One multiplication, no training.
cap.2: In TransformerLens: cache.accumulated_resid(layer=-1, incl_mid=True), then apply_ln_to_stack(..., layer=-1), then multiply by W_U or dot with a logit-difference direction.
cap.3: The LN scale used is the one computed from the real final residual, applied to every layer. That is an approximation: fine for a global scale, and a lens-model gap is information.

cap.1: Poll after every round and plot the answers. On the name task the jury is undecided for nine rounds, then suddenly leans hard towards the right name.
cap.2: In ARENA's IOI exercises the logit difference (right name minus wrong name) read through the lens is flat until layer 9, then jumps. That localises the decision without touching the model.
cap.3: An accumulated-residual lens on the logit-difference direction gives the counterfactual 'delete every later layer'. Curve shape schematic; the layer-9 jump is the reported feature.

chapters.name: Guesses, not echoes

right.title: What GPT-2 shows
lines: the guess is refined, layer by layer

chapters.verdict: The stream is a running prediction almost from the start.

cap.1: The surprise: early polls do not repeat the evidence back. Almost from the first round, the jury is already guessing the verdict and just refining it.
cap.2: nostalgebraist found GPT-2's intermediate layers decode to sensible next-token guesses that converge on the final answer, and almost never to the input tokens themselves.
cap.3: The input representation is discarded within about the first layer; later computation refines a prediction rather than transforming an input (nostalgebraist, LessWrong, 2020).

chapters.name: When the lens lies
chapters.verdict: Check on GPT-2 first. Where the raw lens fails, a tuned lens learns one decoder per layer.

cap.1: The straw poll assumes early notes are written in the same language as the final vote. In GPT-2 that roughly holds. In some other models it does not.
cap.2: Current method: the raw lens, which works well on GPT-2. Research (Belrose et al.) finds it brittle on other families and trains a tuned lens. What you need: the raw lens on GPT-2, tested on a known case.
cap.3: The tuned lens fits an affine probe per layer instead of assuming the identity. Any lens is correlational: it says what layer L encodes, never that L caused it. Patching tests that.

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: Read what a feature or steering vector promotes

cap.1: It is the cheapest look inside a model: no training, no surgery, one multiplication. It tells you roughly where a decision happens, so you know where to dig.
cap.2: Split the same readout by component and you get direct logit attribution. Apply it to an SAE decoder vector and you see which tokens that feature pushes toward.
cap.3: The same W_U projection on a steering vector or SAE latent gives its promoted-token profile with no forward pass: a first check on what an intervention will make the model say.

caption.1: Each bar is a straw poll after one layer: above zero favours the right name. Move the decision layer, then add a late push-back and watch middle polls disagree.
caption.2: The lens reads a running total, so a bar only moves at layers that write along the answer direction. A late negative write makes middle polls disagree with the output: a finding, not a bug.
caption.3: Toy stream: layer d writes +s along the logit-difference direction, layer 11 writes c. Lens(L) is the cumulative sum; DLA would credit d with s and 11 with c. Real curves are messier.

hamming.what: Running an intermediate residual state through the model's own final LayerNorm and unembedding, to read what it would predict if it stopped there.
hamming.when: When you want a cheap first look at where in the stack a prediction forms, before any patching.
hamming.why: It needs no training or intervention, it shows the stream is a running prediction, and where it disagrees with the model, the gap points at what later layers do.

object.title: The polling tower
object.subtitle: Twelve straw polls stacked from the first layer to the last, five candidate words each (schematic, not measured).

knobs.label: Late layers push back towards John

cap.1: Twelve straw polls, one per layer, five candidate words each. Taller means more votes. The shape is schematic, not measured.
cap.2: Each row is a lens distribution after one layer on an IOI-style prompt, restricted to five candidates.
cap.3: Rows: softmax(W_U · LN_final(resid_L)) over five candidates; values schematic, to show the shape of the finding.

cap.1: From the side: the right name barely registers for eight layers, then shoots up around layer 9. That is where the jury decided.
cap.2: The reported IOI result: the lens logit difference is flat until layer 9, then jumps. The lens localises the decision.
cap.3: Localisation without intervention: the jump marks where components writing the answer direction sit. Patching then tests causation.

cap.1: Move the decision earlier and the tower changes shape. The lens would now send you looking for the mechanism in earlier layers.
cap.2: Where the curve moves tells you which layers to patch first.
cap.3: The lens narrows the search space for activation patching; it cannot itself show those layers are necessary.

cap.1: Now the last layers push back towards the wrong name. The middle polls disagree with the final vote, and that gap is a finding.
cap.2: When the lens at layer 10 disagrees with the output, a later component changed the prediction. Information, not a bug.
cap.3: Lens-model disagreement flags late writes along the answer direction, or a basis mismatch; DLA and patching tell them apart.

cap.1: From above, the tower changes colour as it rises: generic guesses first, then one answer, refined rather than invented at the end.
cap.2: Early layers already hold guesses, not copies of the input: the stream is a running prediction.
cap.3: nostalgebraist's observation: after roughly the first layer, the stream lives in prediction space, not input space.

predict.q: What does the logit lens compute at layer 5?

options.t: The final LayerNorm and unembedding applied to layer 5's residual
A newly trained probe for layer 5

predict.why: No training: it borrows the model's own output step. A trained decoder per layer is the tuned lens.

predict.q: The lens at layer 10 favours John, but the model outputs Mary. A bug?

options.t: Not necessarily: a later layer changed the prediction
Yes: the lens must match the output at every layer

predict.why: Where the lens disagrees with the model, the gap is itself a finding about what later layers do.

predict.q: The raw lens decodes to noise on a new model family. Most likely cause?

options.t: Its middle layers are not in W_U's basis

predict.why: The lens assumes a shared basis, which holds for GPT-2 but not everywhere. Test on GPT-2 small first; the tuned lens learns a decoder per layer.

object.where: Any readout that borrows the final decoder early: DLA per component, SAE latents' promoted tokens, steering vectors.
